item.title: Local community pilots solar water project in Kairuku
item.description: A local community in Kairuku, Central,has initiated a solar powered purified water supply project, initiated to improve water supply system during the El Nino period. The solar purified water project is the first to be initiated at Apo Apo community at the Bereina village in ward 18 of the Kairuku Local Level Government constituent
item.content:encoded:
A local community in Kairuku, Central,has initiated a solar powered purified water supply project, initiated to improve water supply system during the El Nino period.

The solar purified water project is the first to be initiated at Apo Apo community at the Bereina village in ward 18 of the Kairuku Local Level Government constituent

The water project is a determination from local communities who took the ownership to trial the project through the tireless efforts of the Buana brothers, namely Emmanuel and famous musician Merfy Buana.

After numerous efforts and commitment towards the project, the Kairuku District Development Authority (KDDA) injected K70,000 to make the project a reality through a submission written to the KDDA by the Buana brothers.

Kairuku MP and Minister for Energy Peter during the official launch of the water project commended the Buana family and the community from initiating the water project to benefit the community at large.

He stressed the ideal importance of taking ownership of initiating projects before receiving support from the government.

He said such approach by the Buana family and the local community of Apo Apo is a testament of creating own community development initiatives.

item.title: Wabag DDA launches ‘rausim kunai putim kapa’ program
item.description: The Wabag District Development Authority of the Enga Province have launched a community housing transformation program called Rausim Kunai Putim Kapa. The aim of the program is to transform pit-roofed homes into durable, modern iron-roof structures.
item.content:encoded:
The Wabag District Development Authority of the Enga Province have launched a community housing transformation program called Rausim Kunai Putim Kapa.

The aim of the program is to transform pit-roofed homes into durable, modern iron-roof structures.

The Rausim Kunai, Putim Kapa program launched by the Wabag DDA on Friday the 12th of this month is an initiative that aims to build durable homes in semi urban and rural communities of the Wabag district where traditional grass thatched roof houses are the common homes.

According to the DDA the initiative has come about because traditional grass thatched roofing homes deteriorate quickly causing health risks and fire hazards.

The vision is to create durable houses with modern materials which create also a cleaner environment.

Important benefits of this program include reduce respiratory issues caused by rotting roof, clean catchment of rainwater through gutters and to tanks, lowers the maintenance costs with thatch roofing which includes the process of thatch harvesting. With iron-roofing homes are protected against torrential rains for decades to come.

The program was launched by the Governor of Enga Province Sir Peter Ipatas along with the Member for Wabag district, Dr. Lino Tom.

Speaking to Dr. Lino following the launching he said the program is also a way to reduce the risk of tribal conflict.

He explained that when individuals in communities feel responsible with a sense of ownership of the modern homes meaning understanding the cost and risk it may take try to build a new house it fosters peace more than disruption.

Eligibility requirements include confirmation of residency within the Wabag District LLG Ward and confirmation of a structure fully framed and ready for roof installation.

Priority is to be given to elderly, widows, low-income families, and vulnerable household.

item.title: Valupai secondary hosts pioneer graduation
item.description: The Saint Joseph Valupai Catholic Secondary School in West New Britain Province has achieved a significant milestone with the passing out of its pioneer batch of Grade 12 students. The school was elevated from a Junior High School to Secondary School in 2022 and has now seen the graduation of twenty-seven pioneer students who passed out in a ceremony held at the school yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
The Saint Joseph Valupai Catholic Secondary School in West New Britain Province has achieved a significant milestone with the passing out of its pioneer batch of Grade 12 students.

The school was elevated from a Junior High School to Secondary School in 2022 and has now seen the graduation of twenty-seven pioneer students who passed out in a ceremony held at the school yesterday.

Governor Sasindran Muthuvel and Member for Talasea, Freddie Reu Kumai were among the dignitaries who officiated at the graduation ceremony.

Saint Joseph Valupai Catholic Secondary School is located in the Ward 8 area of the Talasea Local Level Government and its elevation to secondary status is the brainchild of Talasea MP, Freddie Reu Kumai.

“In 2022, I made a bold statement to graduate the first batch of Grade 12 students in 2026, and this has now happened,”

“To the graduates, you’re a special batch as you’re the pioneers and you carry the dreams and aspirations of Saint Joseph Valupai Catholic Secondary School and the entire Talasea district,” Mr Kumai said.

He also acknowledged the Catholic Diocese of Kimbe under Bishop, Reverend John Bosco Auram for partnering with the government to deliver education services in the Talasea District and especially with the operations of the Saint Joseph Valpuai Catholic Secondary School.

The Talasea District Development Authority Board invested over K5 million in the construction of new facilities to match secondary school standards as alluded to by the Talasea MP.

“We have built quality infrastructure here to ensure this school provides the level of education required for secondary school standards. Infrastructure built here are among the best compared to other secondary schools in the province,” Mr Kumai clarified.

Meanwhile, the West New Britain Provincial Government also provided counterpart funding totaling nearly a million Kina to assist with the construction of new facilities at the school.

This funding went towards the construction of an Administration building, a Science Laboratory and a teacher’s house.

Governor Sasindran Muthuvel said his government is happy to partner with the Talasea DDA Board to improve services in the district and will continue to counter fund the development aspirations of the Talasea MP.

Governor Muthuvel formally commissioned the new teacher’s house after the graduation ceremony.

item.title: Leadership award student to witness the last Parliament sitting
item.description: Mt. Wilhelm secondary school Leadership Award winner Andrew Wena (right) shakes hands with Kumura Foundation representative Willie Yagoi. Wena will travel to Port Moresby to witness the last Parliament sitting of this year, fully sponsored by the Kumura Foundation (NBC News) From a classroom in rural Gembogl, in Simbu straight to the floor of Parliament in Waigani.
item.content:encoded:
Mt. Wilhelm secondary school Leadership Award winner Andrew Wena (right) shakes hands with Kumura Foundation representative Willie Yagoi. Wena will travel to Port Moresby to witness the last Parliament sitting of this year, fully sponsored by the Kumura Foundation (NBC News)

From a classroom in rural Gembogl, in Simbu straight to the floor of Parliament in Waigani.

Andrew Wena, the Leadership Award winner for Mount Wilhelm Secondary School, will travel to Port Moresby to witness the last Parliament sitting of this year.

Wena will also tour the city and visit the office of the Member for Usino Bundi, Vincent Kumura, who is also the Vice Minister Assisting the Prime Minister.

The announcement was made by Willie Yagoi from the Kumura Foundation during the Grade 12 graduation at the Mount Wilhelm Tourist Hotel in Kundiawa today.

Mr Yagoi said the trip will be fully sponsored by the Kumura Foundation, funded by its Director and Member for Usino Bundi, Vincent Kumura.

"This is a prize that goes beyond the classroom. It is a chance for a young man from Simbu to see how the country is run, up close," Mr Yagoi said.

The Kumura Foundation also sponsored K1,000 each to the Science Dux and the Social Science Dux.

"I just tried to lead by example in school, but now I have the chance to see Parliament with my own eyes," he said.

Simbu Governor Noah Kool was also present at the graduation.

Governor Kool spoke about discipline, respect and commitment, the three values he said will decide whether a Grade 12 certificate becomes a successful future, or just a paper on the wall.

School Principal Kaupa Gomna said the school decided to give special treatment to the 2026 Cohorts because they are a special group.

"These are the students who survived the worst of the El Nino. But they stayed, they continued, and they finished their exams," Mr Gomna said.

For Mount Wilhelm Secondary School, this year's graduation was not just about finishing school. It was about survival, history, and what leadership can open.

item.title: Faith builds a new administration building
item.description: The new K3.3 million ELC PNG Hagen district administration and office building that has brought a facelift to the city of Mt Hagen (NBC News) After almost three years of sacrifice, faith and determination, the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Papua New Guinea (ELC PNG) Hagen District has opened a new K3.3 million two-storey administration building in the heart of Mt Hagen city.
item.content:encoded:
The new K3.3 million ELC PNG Hagen district administration and office building that has brought a facelift to the city of Mt Hagen (NBC News)

After almost three years of sacrifice, faith and determination, the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Papua New Guinea (ELC PNG) Hagen District has opened a new K3.3 million two-storey administration building in the heart of Mt Hagen city.

The new building replaces the old structure that had served the church for decades, dating back to the early days of Lutheran missionary work in the Highlands.

The new two-storey ELC PNG Hagen District administration building now stands as a symbol of what can be achieved through faith, unity and perseverance.

For almost three years, members of the Hagen District congregation contributed towards the project through Thanksgiving and Sunday offerings, believing they could build a modern administration center for the church.

Despite the challenges, the congregation did not give up.

Their contributions, together with support from the government and other partners, have now produced this K3.3 million state-of-the-art office building.

"It is hard to get a contractor to build a building like this within a short space of time because contractors have their own demand but through the Grace and God's willing, the two storey was completed and opened and I thank each and every member of ELC Hagen District," says Jacob Lama, building committee treasurer.

He also outlined how the money was spent on the construction of the building.

"The money that you the Christians of ELC Hage district has come up with adds to a sum of K3,371, 020. 30."

"When we see that if we get a contractor alone to do the work, cost will go up than our budgeted cost. So, I held talks with the Building Committee that instead of giving the money to the contractor we should do project management where we did and now, we see the completion and opening of the building at the exact cost of K3,317,809.61 with almost K50,000 remaining that will be used to carry out other unfinished work of the building," outlines treasurer Lama.

The new building replaces the old administration office, which had become worn out after serving the church since the arrival of the first Lutheran missionaries in Mt Hagen.

Head Bishop of ELC PNG, Reverend Jack Urame, also thanked the Christians of the Hagen District for their commitment and sacrifice.

He acknowledged the support from the government towards the work of the Lutheran Church in Papua New Guinea.

"Thank you to the believers of ELC Hagen District for sowing in the work of God and continue to do so for God's Glory and Honour," Bishop Urame adds.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa, who witnessed the opening, also praised the Christians for their commitment to the project.

Governor Rapa said the building is a reflection of the blessings received through the congregation's faith and giving.

He said the new structure has also given Mt Hagen city a facelift and will provide a lasting home for the church's administration.

"God has never ceased to bless us every day and I want to take this time to thank the Christians of ELC Hagen District to take this step of faith and sacrifice to make sure that you give towards the work of God.

"This state of art two storey administration building has now give a facelift to the city of Mt Hagen and I want to say thank you to the congregation of Hagen District, its 16 circuits, Mt Hagen City Authority under the Chairmanship of Hagen Open MP William Duma, the provincial government and others who have participated in one or the way to see this happening," said Rapa.

item.title: Madang health facilities get starlink connectivity
item.description: UNFPA engaged contractors preparing to install a starlink set at Bunabun health centre in the Sumkar district (NBC News) The Madang Provincial Health Authority has started rolling out highspeed internet connectivity to its health facilities with the installation of Starlink, thanks to the assistance of the United Nations Population Fund or UNFPA.
item.content:encoded:
UNFPA engaged contractors preparing to install a starlink set at Bunabun health centre in the Sumkar district (NBC News)

The Madang Provincial Health Authority has started rolling out highspeed internet connectivity to its health facilities with the installation of Starlink, thanks to the assistance of the United Nations Population Fund or UNFPA.

The installation of Starlink will improve communication links for all Madang PHA facilities in the six districts and the provincial hospital.

Three district health facilities, including the main provincial hospital were the first to be connected this week.

The first was installed at Gusap, the second at Daigul, then Bunabun and the provincial hospital.

Chief Executive Officer of Madang PHA, Dr Martin Daimen has thanked UNFPA for the assistance, highlighting that communication is one of many other factors that are very important to the delivery of health services.

"For any development to take place, certain factors must be addressed, including communication. For health, it's one of the critical areas, just like water, power, land and human resource. That is why the MaPHA management and board, we've started this pilot project.

"We have successfully installed Starlink at Gusap, Daigul, Bunabun and the provincial hospital without any difficulties with the help of a UNFPA- engaged contractor. The other main focus now is to have solar power installed for those facilities without electricity connectivity," Dr Daimen said.

He added that Starlink is now bridging the geographical terrains of the province. It will make information readily available.

"It will help our nurses and doctors deliver very vital information, skills and knowledge to our health workers in the rural and remote areas when needed, to attend to patients, such as in childbirth," he stated.

Board Chairman of MaPHA, Dr Boga Figa communication has always been one of the board's priorities when they assumed office in 2024.

"When we took office in September of 2024, one of the main agendas I asked about was whether Madang PHA had an ICT plan and that still stands. We can have an ICT policy but what plan will the policy drive. I thank our partners because ICT is one of the board's main agendas.

"I come from an industry background where ICT plays everything, drives everything. You can be here and be connected to Bogia or even Moresby.

"ICT makes sure everything is controlled, monitored, including standards. I have visited hospitals in advanced economies where information is readily available at the fingertips. This program will enable our patients and health workers even in the very remotest locations to communicate with doctors and nurses at the main hospital," Dr Figa said.

Figa assured the program has the board's full backing to make sure it reaches all corners of Madang Province.

On behalf of the Madang Provincial Administration, John Sigara, Director Planning applauded UNFPA for stepping in to assist MaPHA improve communication accessibility with the rural health facilities throughout the province.

item.title: Poor Lae-Bulolo highway concerns businesses
item.description: The poor condition of the Lae-Bulolo Highway is raising concerns for businesses that rely on the road to transport goods and agricultural produce between rural communities and Lae. Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry President John Byrne says some sections of the highway, particularly beyond Gebensis towards Zenag, are in poor condition and need urgent attention.
item.content:encoded:
The poor condition of the Lae-Bulolo Highway is raising concerns for businesses that rely on the road to transport goods and agricultural produce between rural communities and Lae.

Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry President John Byrne says some sections of the highway, particularly beyond Gebensis towards Zenag, are in poor condition and need urgent attention.

Byrne says he travelled along the highway over the weekend and noticed the road becoming rougher as motorists travelled further towards Zenag.

He says the highway is an important route for businesses, farmers and communities who depend on it to move their goods and supplies.

The dry weather and El Niño conditions have also increased dust along the road, creating problems for motorists, passengers and people walking along the highway.

Byrne says the dust is affecting people's health, particularly those who are exposed to it every day.

He says a committee representing the Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry is working with contractors and other stakeholders to find ways to speed up road repairs.

However, funding remains a major challenge in addressing the road conditions.

Byrne says improving the highway is important for businesses and communities that depend on the road for transport and access to markets.

item.title: Casa to get repairs in Indonesia
item.description: PNG Defence Force CASA CN-235 aircraft, P2-502 ready to depart for Indonesia (NBC News) Papua New Guinea is taking steps to restore its military air transport capability after years of relying on external support to move personnel and equipment.
item.content:encoded:
PNG Defence Force CASA CN-235 aircraft, P2-502 ready to depart for Indonesia (NBC News)

Papua New Guinea is taking steps to restore its military air transport capability after years of relying on external support to move personnel and equipment.

The PNG Defence Force CASA CN-235 aircraft, P2-502, has departed for Indonesia for major servicing and a complete overhaul under the CASA Recovery Programme.

Prime Minister James Marape says restoring the aircraft will strengthen national security, border protection and disaster response.

PNG Defence Force Commander Rear Admiral Philip Polewara says restoring the aircraft will strengthen the military's ability to safeguard the country and assist communities during disasters.

The aircraft is expected to return to PNG in time to support next year's General Elections.
